prompt.context: Your client is a BIG-3 car manufacturer from the US. The client is interested in acquiring a leading rental car agency in the US.
prompt.question: What key questions would you answer to help the client make a decision? And is this acquisition a good idea?

framework: What is the objective behind the acquisition?
How is the target performing as a stand-alone company? (growth rate, profits, industry growth)
What are the synergies between the client and the target? (operational and financial synergies; can the target be disciplined and improved?)
What are the risks in this acquisition?
Is there a cultural fit between the client and the target?
Is there a competitive bid? Will the client have more synergies than if a competitor acquires the target?
The financial details of the acquisition — how much will the client pay and do they have funding?
Do the managers executing this deal have experience in deal-making and post-merger integration?

questions.prompt: What are the possible operating synergies of the acquisition?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate identifies at least 2 revenue synergies and 2 cost synergies. Guide discussion toward operating synergies — both the positives and the negatives.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the operating synergies (revenue and cost) and potential risks of the acquisition?

categories.name: Revenue synergies
ideas: Rental car company becomes an assured customer, boosting the manufacturer's sales and market share
If the rental company has strong international presence, it helps the client expand and establish a foothold in international markets
Customers who frequently rent the client's cars are more likely to purchase them for personal use, inducing future demand
Opportunity to rent new model cars and induce demand for new products
Staying closely in touch with customers helps understand requirements, make quick changes, and generate ideas for new product development

categories.name: Cost synergies
ideas: Reduction of corporate, administrative costs and overhead
Both companies have claims processing divisions that can be merged to reduce costs

categories.name: Potential risks
ideas: How will other rental car companies react? Competitors may refuse to buy the manufacturer's cars
Competitors may stop supplying their cars to the acquired rental company

recommendation: Evaluate whether the strategic objective (market share, international expansion, demand induction) justifies the acquisition premium
Confirm that identified synergies — particularly the assured customer relationship and claims-processing consolidation — are realizable and material
risks: Competitor rental companies retaliating by dropping the manufacturer's fleet
Competitor auto manufacturers withdrawing supply from the acquired rental agency
Cultural mismatch between a manufacturing organization and a service/rental business
Overpaying if a competitive bidder drives up the price
next_steps: Quantify revenue and cost synergies vs. acquisition price
Assess competitive bid landscape and alternative acquirers
Evaluate management team's M&A and post-merger integration experience
